title: improv·artist · explosive (Cai Guo-Qiang)
mutation_directive: improv artist: explosive via Cai Guo-Qiang

improv_extras.practice: gunpowder drawings, fireworks, flash and char; ephemeral pyrotechnics

v1.feedback: The growth-then-detonate-then-char cycle is a genuine reading of Cai Guo-Qiang and the dual particle system earns its complexity, but the bursts risk reading as additive-blended noise blobs once several chain detonations overlap — clamp simultaneous live burst particles or fade older shells faster so each detonation has a distinct silhouette. The camera target is fixed at y=5 while the tower keeps rising past frame; auto-track the growth centroid or slowly dolly the camera upward so the form stays >30% of viewport throughout the piece. Consider giving burst particles a short bright-to-ember color ramp with a tail fade rather than uniform spherical scatter, so the explosions read as directional flash-and-char marks instead of isotropic sparkle.

v2.feedback: The build→detonate→char cycle genuinely maps Cai Guo-Qiang's practice onto the 5gm tower form, and the one-burst-at-a-time constraint keeps silhouette legible through detonation events. The char particles likely vanish against the 0x0a0c0f background since their terminal color (0.12,0.10,0.09) is near-black — Cai's work leaves visible scorch marks, so the char phase should settle to a warm dark brown (~0.25,0.15,0.08) with a small persistent alpha floor (0.08–0.12) so residue accumulates as a soot ghost of past bursts. Consider giving burst particles a brief directional gravity pull after the radial flash so they arc downward like real pyrotechnic fallout rather than expanding spherically, which would read more as explosion and less as particle-sim default.
